questiontext.text: The number of structurally distinct binary trees with n nodes is given by which sequence?

feedback.text: Correct — the count is the nth Catalan number.
No — Fibonacci counts a different recurrence, not tree shapes.
No — 2^n overcounts; not every bit pattern is a valid tree shape.
No — n! counts permutations, not distinct tree structures.

generalfeedback.text: The number of distinct binary tree shapes on n nodes (and distinct BSTs over n keys) is the nth Catalan number.

questiontext.text: Which closed-form expression gives the nth Catalan number Cn?

feedback.text: Correct — the central binomial coefficient divided by n+1.
No — that is not the Catalan formula.
No — the numerator is the binomial C(2n, n), not 2^n.
No — you divide by n+1, not multiply.

generalfeedback.text: C_n = C(2n, n) / (n + 1); equivalently C_n = (2n)! / ((n+1)! n!).

questiontext.text: How many structurally distinct binary trees exist with 3 nodes (i.e. C3)?

feedback.text: Correct — C_3 = 5.
No — 6 = 3!, the number of key orderings, not distinct tree shapes.
No — there are more than 3 distinct shapes for 3 nodes.
No — 2^3 overcounts; the answer is 5.

generalfeedback.text: C_0=1, C_1=1, C_2=2, C_3=5, C_4=14, C_5=42; so with 3 nodes there are 5 distinct binary tree shapes.

questiontext.text: Which recurrence generates the Catalan numbers (splitting on the root's subtree sizes)?

feedback.text: Correct — sum over the left subtree size i and right subtree size n−i.
No — that is the Fibonacci recurrence.
No — that generates factorials.
No — that generates powers of two.

generalfeedback.text: Fixing the root, the left subtree has i nodes and the right has n−i, so C_{n+1} = Σ C_i·C_{n−i}.

questiontext.text: The number of distinct binary search trees over n distinct keys equals the nth Catalan number.

feedback.text: Correct — each distinct shape corresponds to exactly one BST over the sorted keys.
The count of distinct BSTs is indeed the nth Catalan number.

questiontext.text: The number of distinct binary tree shapes with n nodes equals n! (n factorial).

feedback.text: No — it is the nth Catalan number, which is smaller than n! for n > 2.
Correct — it is the Catalan number, not n!.

questiontext.text: The sequence 1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, ... that counts binary tree shapes is called the ______ numbers.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.

questiontext.text: Which of the following are counted by the nth Catalan number? (select all that apply)

answer.text: The number of distinct binary search trees over n keys

feedback.text: Yes — one per distinct tree shape.

answer.text: The number of valid strings of n balanced pairs of parentheses

feedback.text: Yes — this is a classic Catalan interpretation.

answer.text: The number of permutations of n distinct elements

feedback.text: No — that is n!, not Catalan.

answer.text: The number of subsets of an n-element set

feedback.text: No — that is 2^n, not Catalan.

generalfeedback.text: Catalan counts binary tree shapes, distinct BSTs, balanced-parenthesis strings, full binary trees with n+1 leaves, and polygon triangulations — but not permutations (n!) or subsets (2^n).
